feature: ordinary Channel Health Watch admission lifecycle

reference.readiness_contract: doc/wait-for-ready.md: CONNECTING does not itself fail either RPC mode; TRANSIENT_FAILURE rejects fail-fast calls and queues wait-for-ready calls
reference.independent_health_peer: Node HTTP/2 with literal gRPC envelopes and protobuf Health payloads

behavior.worker_ownership: worker termination destroys the reconnecting Watch, its private Channel, dedicated connection and service-name copy before the parent Channel is destroyed
behavior.retry: Watch retry events publish a known rejection; unary, streaming and duplex fail-fast starts return ConnectionUnavailable; wait-for-ready remains queued until SERVING or UNIMPLEMENTED
behavior.initial_admission: pending initial health admission uses only the caller deadline or cancellation for both RPC modes; no implicit five-second timeout
behavior.cancellation: cancelWaits publishes cancellation and increments the health Sync generation; admission checks it before each state scan; resetCancellation after joining restores admission

cpp_debug.scope: bounded RPC health admission and Watch teardown on parent shutdown, plus existing shared/streaming/compression/metadata/deadline/cancellation/soak/proxy/failover matrix

regressions: UNIMPLEMENTED peer observes EOF on its dedicated Watch connection while the parent Channel continues two business calls
UNAVAILABLE Watch rejects all three fail-fast starts before any business connection is opened; a succeeding Watch restores a waiting unary call
a clock advancing ten seconds per read cannot impose a hidden initial-health deadline on either RPC mode
explicit caller deadline reaches the wake primitive unchanged and Canceled preserves the admission state
a real unbounded unary caller is parked, cancelWaits wakes it with Canceled, then resetCancellation and SERVING restore a successful call

verification_commands: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='health gate' -Dtest-filter='reconnecting health Watch' --summary all
remaining_scope: Broader composite/xDS integration and long-duration/high-concurrency stability evidence remain open for the overall protocol-library goal.
